solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Request for help servant uttered? That's correct

indicators.note: uttered means the word for the servant is spoken, and its sound is what goes in

parts.note: a maid is a female servant
ay (aye) is the word of assent, yes, that's right

explanation.surface: Someone calls a servant, asks for help, and gets an approving reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uttered' makes MAID be heard as MAYD; AY is a spelling of aye, 'yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio distress call used by ships and aircraft is an urgent plea for rescue.

clue.text: Mother keeps longing for actor, so called…

indicators.note: keeps means the word for mother holds the longing inside it

parts.note: mum is mother
an itch is a longing, a craving

explanation.surface: Mother harbours a yearning for a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots run on into 2-down: Robert Mitchum played in westerns, as did John Wayne, nicknamed 'Duke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Mitchum was a Hollywood film star of the 1940s to 1960s.

clue.text: … 'Duke' in the old westerns, say? Surprisingly he's no longer of interest

indicators.note: in means the duke's letter is set inside the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters of westerns say are jumbled unexpectedly

explanation.surface: Following 1-down: the Duke of old westerns turns out to be forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' evokes John Wayne but is just D. 'Surprisingly' rearranges WESTERNS SAY into STERAYSNEWS; YE goes before it and D goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stale, like an old newspaper, is a figure for a person who is now forgotten.

clue.text: Picking up receiver when we phone about noon

indicators.note: about means the word for when goes around the noon letter

parts.note: as means when
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Someone takes a call at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the handset is how one replies to a telephone call.

clue.text: Tennis player's hard slog knocking out finalist

indicators.note: the finalist here is the final letter, which is knocked off the word for a hard slog

parts.note: graft is British slang for hard work

explanation.surface: A tennis player toils away, then beats a finalist in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finalist' is not a player: it is the final letter, T, removed from GRAFT. Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf, the German champion, is one of the great female players of the sport.

clue.text: After fog's lifted, soldiers attack

indicators.note: after puts the soldiers following the lifted fog
lifted in a down clue means the word fog is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Once the fog clears, the troops launch an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' looks like weather but reverses FOG to GOF.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is an idiom meaning to attack them.

clue.text: A college servant at Oxford dismissed university course

indicators.note: dismissed means the university letter is sent out of the servant

parts.note: a scout is a college servant at Oxford University

explanation.surface: An Oxford college servant is sacked from a university course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is not a degree but a racecourse; Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse of Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England.

clue.text: Capital family has invested in South Africa

parts.note: kin is family

indicators.note: invested in means the word has is put inside South Africa

explanation.surface: A family has put its money into South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests money, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinshasa is the chief city and seat of government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

clue.text: Prodigal gets home, fits in: that shows how things are today

definitions.text: that shows how things are today

indicators.note: prodigal means wasteful and wayward, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: The prodigal son returns home and settles in, a sign of modern life.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator of current trends is an idiom for something typical of the present era.

clue.text: Plan adopted by Stalin tentatively

indicators.note: adopted by means the letters are taken in by the words Stalin tentatively

explanation.surface: Stalin cautiously took up a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention or purpose is what someone means to do, a synonym for plan.

clue.text: To crack regiment, they're doggedly tough fighters

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is the British Army's elite special forces regiment

explanation.surface: Tough fighters manage to break into an army regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective 'elite' qualifying the regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tosa is a Japanese breed of mastiff bred for dog fighting, so 'doggedly' is literal.

clue.text: Details ultimately unknown about sort of therapy one's given for viral illness

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go around the therapy and the one

parts.note: info is short for information, details
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word unknown

explanation.surface: Details of some therapy given for a viral illness remain unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: INFO plus N (end of 'unknown') makes INFON, which goes 'about' ECT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus causes a disease by invading the body, which is an infectious condition.

clue.text: As you say, they make better herding dogs

indicators.note: as you say means the clue's phrase is to be spoken and heard

parts.note: healers are people who cure, who make others better

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that certain dogs improve things.
explanation.walkthrough: Heelers, such as the Australian cattle dog, drive livestock by nipping at their heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle dogs that nip at the heels of livestock to move them are known by this name.

clue.text: English detachment returning initially on train

indicators.note: initially says the word for on is placed at the very start

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: returning means the word for a detachment is read backwards

parts.note: a unit is a detachment of soldiers

explanation.surface: An English military detachment returns home by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is not a railway: it is the followers of a dignitary, as in a royal train.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a group of attendants following an important person, which is an entourage.

clue.text: Singer very keen to appear with fiddle before top celebrities

indicators.note: before puts the fiddle ahead of the celebrities

parts.note: mad about something means very keen on it
to rig is to fiddle, manipulate dishonestly
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: An eager violinist performs ahead of the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a violin but means RIG, to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of unaccompanied Renaissance part-songs is someone who sings.

clue.text: Suggested adult should be hauled out and charged

indicators.note: hauled out means the adult letter is pulled out of the word for suggested

parts.note: indicated means suggested
A is adult, the old film classification

explanation.surface: A grown-up is hauled out of court and charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To be formally accused of a crime in law is to be charged.

clue.text: Open-air restaurant with rickety gate leading to forest

indicators.note: leading to puts the jumbled gate ahead of the forest
rickety means shaky, so the letters of gate are rearranged

parts.note: Arden is a forest, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: An outdoor café with a broken-down gate leading into woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' rearranges GATE to TEAG.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor café where refreshments are served among plants is an alfresco eatery.

clue.text: Feasts taken regularly could make you so

indicators.note: taken regularly means only every other letter of the word feasts is used

explanation.surface: A warning that eating banquets often will make you plump.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a health warning, with 'so' standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating at regular banquets would leave a person overweight, the state the clue alludes to.

clue.text: Without piano introduction perform song

indicators.note: without means a letter is taken away from the word for perform

parts.note: to play is to perform

indicators.note: introduction points to the first letter of the word piano

explanation.surface: A singer performs a song with no piano intro.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a ballad or narrative poem meant to be sung.

clue.text: Strong urge one has to enrol in Liberal party

indicators.note: enrol in means the one is placed within the letters for Liberal and party

parts.note: a do is a party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to join the Liberal party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political but means a celebration, DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive or desire, a powerful urge.

clue.text: Old man has South African currency and francs among hoard

indicators.note: among means the currency and francs go inside the word for hoard

parts.note: to gather is to collect, hoard
the rand is the currency of South Africa
F is the abbreviation for francs

explanation.surface: An old man is stockpiling rand and francs.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Old man' can be slang for a father, and a parent's father is an elderly male relative.

clue.text: Hit by car's exhaust?

definitions.meaning: a pedestrian struck by a vehicle has been knocked over
to exhaust is to deplete, wear out

explanation.walkthrough: 'car's exhaust' suggests a tailpipe; the 's is only a link, and 'exhaust' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: knocked over by a vehicle, and to tire out or deplete gradually.

clue.text: Powerful tool was misused by group of people

indicators.note: by means next to, so the scrambled letters sit beside the group

parts.note: a band is a group of people

indicators.note: misused means the letters of was are put to wrong use, rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful tool was mishandled by a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A power saw with a continuous toothed steel loop is a heavy-duty workshop tool.

clue.text: Fibre used for making sails

indicators.note: used for making means the letters of sails are worked into a new word

explanation.surface: A fibre for making sails.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Spent year south of the river

indicators.note: south of in a down clue means the year sits below the river

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: A year was spent south of the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' looks like a verb but is the adjective, exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent as an adjective means exhausted, tired out.

clue.text: Guitarist applauded in auditorium, appearing at last

indicators.note: at last puts the word for appearing at the end
in an auditorium the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: clapped means applauded
on means appearing, performing on stage

explanation.surface: A guitarist is cheered in the hall when he finally comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAPT is how 'clapped' sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton is a famous British rock and blues guitar player.

clue.text: In time, towns developed in southern Florida?

indicators.note: in means the scrambled towns go inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a time

indicators.note: developed means the letters of towns are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Over time, towns grew up in the south of Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges TOWNS to OWNST. The question mark marks Florida as only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: American usage for the part of a state away from its big city, often its south.

clue.text: Film that's no talkie, love

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak, so no talker
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A silent movie, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talkie' suggests sound film, but 'no talkie' means DUMB, mute.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1941 animated feature about a flying elephant is a well-known movie.

clue.text: Trick used by employers

indicators.note: used by means the letters are found within the word employers

explanation.surface: Bosses deploy a crafty tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning manoeuvre or tactic is a ruse, a synonym for trick.

clue.text: Concert interval?

definitions.meaning: in concert means in agreement, acting together
in music, two notes of the same pitch form the zero interval

explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' suggests a performance but means agreement, as in 'acting in concert'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together is agreement, and the same-pitch musical interval shares this name.
